paper: ai-and-society/The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity. Evidence from GitHub Copilot
reason: A controlled experiment on AI's effect on developer productivity and careers is an economic effect of AI, not a study of LLM methods or coding agents.
summary: GitHub Copilot productivity experiment: developers with the AI pair programmer implemented an HTTP server in JavaScript 55.8% faster than the control group, with heterogeneous effects suggesting it could help people move into software development careers.

paper: data-centric-ml/augmentation-and-synthetic-data/Fake it till you make it. Learning transferable representations from synthetic ImageNet clones
reason: The paper studies training image classifiers on Stable Diffusion-generated synthetic data instead of real images, which is synthetic training data outside LLM pretraining.
summary: ImageNet-SD: synthetic ImageNet clones generated by Stable Diffusion from class names alone close a large part of the gap to real-image training on classification and match real data for transfer.

paper: data-centric-ml/data-quality-and-shift/Do ImageNet Classifiers Generalize to ImageNet
reason: A test-set replication study showing accuracy drops under a subtle distribution shift between original and newly collected test data, which is the dataset-shift scope.
summary: New CIFAR-10 and ImageNet test sets built by following the original creation processes: accuracy drops 3%–15% on CIFAR-10 and 11%–14% on ImageNet, attributed to slightly harder images and not to adaptive overfitting, while gains on the original test sets translate to larger gains on the new ones.

paper: data-centric-ml/labels-and-annotation/The Perspectivist Paradigm Shift. Assumptions and Challenges of Capturing Human Labels
reason: A position paper on annotator disagreement and label aggregation in the data labeling pipeline, which is the core of the annotation folder's scope.
summary: Perspectivist labeling: a position paper examining assumptions about the causes of annotator disagreement, treating it as information rather than noise, with recommendations for the data labeling pipeline.

paper: data-centric-ml/weak-supervision/Snorkel. Rapid Training Data Creation with Weak Supervision
reason: Snorkel is the canonical programmatic-labelling system, named in this folder's scope.
summary: Snorkel: labeling functions with unknown accuracies denoised via data programming, letting experts build models 2.8x faster and coming within an average 3.60% of large hand-curated training sets.

paper: deep-learning/A continual learning survey. Defying forgetting in classification tasks
reason: Continual learning and catastrophic forgetting in neural classifiers is a general deep-learning training topic; no subfolder covers continual learning, so the parent folder is used.
summary: Continual learning survey: a taxonomy of task-incremental classification methods, a framework for continually determining the stability-plasticity trade-off, and an experimental comparison of 11 methods and 4 baselines on Tiny Imagenet, iNaturalist and a sequence of recognition datasets.

paper: deep-learning/architectures/Going Deeper with Convolutions
reason: A core CNN architecture (Inception/GoogLeNet); the scope covers CNNs and their building blocks, and it is an architecture paper rather than a vision task paper.
summary: Inception/GoogLeNet: a 22-layer CNN that increases depth and width at a constant computational budget, setting the state of the art for classification and detection at ILSVRC'14.

paper: deep-learning/efficiency-and-compression/Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
reason: The paper's core contribution is knowledge distillation from BERT into a small BiLSTM, which fits the general distillation folder better than the BERT-era encoders folder or LLM efficiency.
summary: BERT distilled into a single-layer BiLSTM (and a siamese variant for sentence pairs): comparable to ELMo on paraphrasing, NLI and sentiment classification with roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

paper: experimentation-and-metrics/ab-testing/Trustworthy online controlled experiments. five puzzling outcomes explained
reason: Lessons on pitfalls and trustworthy analysis of online controlled experiments at scale, which is exactly this folder's scope.
summary: Trustworthy online controlled experiments: five puzzling outcomes from Bing experiments traced to root causes in the OEC, click tracking, effect trends, experiment length and power, and carryover effects.

paper: experimentation-and-metrics/causal-inference/A Large Scale Benchmark for Individual Treatment Effect Prediction and Uplift Modeling
reason: A dataset and benchmark for uplift modeling and individual treatment effect prediction, which the causal-inference folder's scope names directly (uplift, counterfactual estimation).
summary: Criteo uplift benchmark: 13.9 million samples from several randomized control trials, 210x larger than prior datasets, with uplift metrics, synthetic response surfaces and baseline UM/ITE comparisons.

paper: experimentation-and-metrics/metric-design/Deconfounding User Satisfaction Estimation from Response Rate Bias
reason: A survey-trained satisfaction model feeding the ranker of a large-scale production recommender, debiased for survey response rate; the recommender setting is where a reader would look, ahead of generic causal inference or metric design.
summary: Response-rate deconfounding: inverse propensity weighting in a shared-bottom multi-task network (satisfaction plus response-rate tasks) corrects survey-trained satisfaction models for users responding more often when they are satisfied.

paper: experimentation-and-metrics/variance-reduction/Consistent Transformation of Ratio Metrics for Efficient Online Controlled Experiments
reason: Sensitivity improvement for A/B-test ratio metrics, combined with regression adjustment, matches the variance-reduction folder's scope of CUPED and other sensitivity improvements.
summary: Ratio metric transformation: rewrites a ratio criterion as the average of a user-level metric so user-level sensitivity techniques apply, with guarantees of preserved directionality and significance level and up to +34% sensitivity rate improvement when combined with the best known regression adjustment on hundreds of large-scale search-engine A/B tests.

paper: generative-models/gans-and-vaes/Perceptual Losses for Real-Time Style Transfer and Super-Resolution
reason: Feed-forward CNN image generation (style transfer, super-resolution) from the pre-diffusion era; the closest fit is the folder covering 'other pre-diffusion generative models', as vision covers architectures and recognition tasks rather than image synthesis.
summary: Perceptual losses: feed-forward image transformation networks trained on high-level features from pretrained networks instead of per-pixel loss match Gatys et al. style transfer quality three orders of magnitude faster and give visually pleasing super-resolution.

paper: graphs/graph-embeddings/Fast and Accurate Network Embeddings via Very Sparse Random Projection
reason: FastRP is a projection-based node embedding method, named explicitly in this folder's scope alongside DeepWalk and node2vec.
summary: FastRP: node embeddings from a degree-normalized transitive similarity matrix reduced by very sparse random projection, over 4,000 times faster than DeepWalk and node2vec at comparable or better accuracy.

paper: graphs/graph-neural-networks/A Comprehensive Survey on Graph Neural Networks
reason: A survey of GNN architectures, which this folder's scope names directly (GNN architectures and surveys).
summary: GNN survey: a taxonomy dividing graph neural networks into recurrent, convolutional, graph autoencoder and spatial-temporal categories, with applications, open-source code, benchmark data sets and research directions.

paper: interpretability/explainability/Grad-CAM. Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-based Localization
reason: Grad-CAM is a saliency-style feature attribution method for explaining CNN decisions, which is exactly this folder's scope.
summary: Grad-CAM: gradients of a target concept flowing into the final convolutional layer give a coarse class-discriminative localization map for a wide variety of CNN models without architectural changes or re-training.

paper: interpretability/mechanistic/Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
reason: Circuit analysis of transformer LLMs through MLP sublayers using transcoders is squarely mechanistic interpretability (circuits, features).
summary: Transcoders: wider, sparsely-activating MLP replacements that enable weights-based circuit analysis through MLP sublayers, factorizing circuits into input-dependent and input-invariant terms and performing at least on par with SAEs on 120M, 410M and 1.4B-parameter models.

paper: llm/agents/Reflexion. Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
reason: A framework for LLM agents that learn from trial-and-error via verbal self-reflection; the episodic memory buffer is a component, but the paper's core is the agent method.
summary: Reflexion: agents reinforce themselves without weight updates by verbally reflecting on task feedback and storing the reflections in an episodic memory buffer, reaching 91% pass@1 on HumanEval versus 80% for GPT-4.

paper: llm/architecture/Byte Latent Transformer. Patches Scale Better Than Tokens
reason: A byte-level LLM architecture that replaces fixed-vocabulary tokenization with dynamic patches, which the llm/architecture scope names directly (tokenization and byte-level models).
summary: Byte Latent Transformer: a byte-level LLM that groups bytes into dynamically sized patches segmented by next-byte entropy, matching tokenization-based models at scale (up to 8B parameters and 4T training bytes) with better inference efficiency and robustness.

paper: llm/architecture/efficient-attention-and-long-context/Efficient Attention. Attention with Linear Complexities
reason: Proposes a linear-complexity attention mechanism, which is the scope of the efficient-attention folder even though the experiments are on vision tasks.
summary: Efficient Attention: a mechanism equivalent to dot-product attention with linear rather than quadratic memory and compute, improving object detection and instance segmentation on MS-COCO 2017 and reaching state-of-the-art stereo depth estimation on Scene Flow.

paper: llm/architecture/recurrent-and-state-space/RWKV. Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
reason: RWKV is a recurrent alternative to attention for language models, named explicitly in this folder's scope.
summary: RWKV: a linear-attention architecture formulated as either a Transformer or an RNN, giving parallel training and constant-cost inference, scaled to 14 billion parameters and performing on par with similarly sized Transformers.

paper: llm/context/Retrieval meets Long Context Large Language Models
reason: The paper compares retrieval augmentation with long-context extension and shows retrieval helps at every window size, so a reader would look for it under RAG.
summary: Retrieval meets Long Context LLMs: a 4K-context LLM with simple retrieval matches a 16K-context finetuned LLM at much less computation, and retrieval-augmented Llama2-70B-32k beats GPT-3.5-turbo-16k and Davinci003 on average over nine long context tasks.

paper: llm/efficiency/LLM Pruning and Distillation in Practice. The Minitron Approach
reason: Compresses LLMs via structured pruning plus distillation, which is exactly the scope of the LLM efficiency folder.
summary: Minitron: structured depth or width pruning plus distillation, preceded by a teacher-correction fine-tune for when the original pretraining data is unavailable, compresses Mistral NeMo 12B to 8B and Llama 3.1 8B to 4B.

paper: llm/evaluation/benchmarks/Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
reason: Proposes a new evaluation metric (50%-task-completion time horizon) calibrated against timed human experts, which is evaluation methodology rather than a new benchmark or agent design.
summary: METR time horizons: the 50%-task-completion time horizon, the human time for tasks AI completes with 50% success, is around 110 minutes for frontier models such as o3 and has doubled approximately every seven months since 2019.

paper: llm/evaluation/methods/Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
reason: HELM is a broad benchmark of LLM capabilities across scenarios and metrics, which is what this folder holds.
summary: HELM: a living benchmark that measures 7 metrics (accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, efficiency) across 16 core scenarios for 30 language models on 42 scenarios in total, raising average core-scenario coverage per model from 17.9% to 96.0%.

paper: llm/foundation-models/NVIDIA Nemotron 3. Efficient and Open Intelligence
reason: A model-family white paper (Nano, Super, Ultra) covering architecture, training and release, which fits the folder for model families and technical reports better than any single-technique folder.
summary: Nemotron 3: an open model family (Nano, Super, Ultra) on a Mixture-of-Experts hybrid Mamba–Transformer architecture with up to 1M-token context, post-trained with multi-environment RL for reasoning and tool use.

paper: llm/personalization/benchmarks/LaMP. When Large Language Models Meet Personalization
reason: LaMP is a benchmark for training and evaluating personalized LLM outputs, which matches the personalization benchmarks folder.
summary: LaMP: a personalization benchmark of seven tasks (three text classification, four text generation) with multiple entries per user profile, where retrieval augmentation from the profile helps both zero-shot and fine-tuned models.

paper: llm/personalization/methods/A Roadmap to Pluralistic Alignment
reason: A framework for how LLMs should represent diverse values — spectrum of responses, steering to perspectives, population calibration — fits model behaviour, specs and steering better than any specific post-training method folder.
summary: Pluralistic alignment roadmap: formalizes Overton, steerable and distributional pluralism plus three benchmark classes (multi-objective, trade-off steerable, jury-pluralistic), with evidence that standard alignment may reduce distributional pluralism.

paper: llm/personalization/user-modelling/RecToM. A Benchmark for Evaluating Machine Theory of Mind in LLM-based Conversational Recommender
reason: A benchmark for inferring users' mental states (theory of mind) in LLM recommendation dialogues, which fits benchmarks for user understanding more specifically than the general LLM benchmarks or recommender folders.
summary: RecToM: a theory-of-mind benchmark for LLM conversational recommenders covering cognitive inference and behavioral prediction, where state-of-the-art LLMs partly recognize mental states but struggle to track evolving intentions and align dialogue strategies with them.

paper: llm/post-training/Large Language Model Post-Training. A Unified View of Off-Policy and On-Policy Learning
reason: A survey spanning SFT, preference optimization, RL and distillation, so it belongs in the parent post-training folder rather than any single-method subfolder.
summary: Post-training survey: a unified framework that splits methods into off-policy and on-policy learning by trajectory provenance and reads them through three roles — effective support expansion, policy reshaping and behavioral consolidation.

paper: llm/post-training/data/Nemotron-4 340B Technical Report
reason: A technical report releasing a model family (base, instruct, reward), which is exactly the scope of foundation-models.
summary: Nemotron-4 340B: an open-access base, instruct and reward model family sized for a single 8-GPU DGX H100 in FP8, aligned with over 98% synthetic data and released with its synthetic data generation pipeline.

paper: llm/post-training/fine-tuning/LoRA. Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
reason: LoRA is the parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that this folder's scope names explicitly.
summary: LoRA: freezing pretrained weights and training injected low-rank decomposition matrices cuts trainable parameters by 10,000 times and GPU memory by 3 times versus fine-tuning GPT-3 175B with Adam, matching or beating full fine-tuning with no additional inference latency.

paper: llm/post-training/preference-learning/Unpacking DPO and PPO. Disentangling Best Practices for Learning from Preference Feedback
reason: A systematic comparison of DPO and PPO, reward models and preference data for preference-based learning, which is exactly this folder's scope.
summary: Unpacking DPO and PPO: across four components of preference learning, better preference data matters most (up to 8% in instruction following and truthfulness), then the algorithm (PPO beats DPO by up to 2.5% in math and 1.2% in general domains), then reward models, then unlabeled policy prompts.

paper: llm/post-training/rl-for-reasoning/Beyond the 80 20 Rule. High-Entropy Minority Tokens Drive Effective Reinforcement Learning for LLM
reason: An analysis of RLVR mechanisms and an improved RLVR training method for reasoning models, which is exactly this folder's scope.
summary: High-entropy forking tokens: restricting RLVR policy gradients to the 20% highest-entropy tokens matches full-gradient updates on Qwen3-8B and beats them on Qwen3-32B (+11.04 on AIME'25, +7.71 on AIME'24), while training on the 80% lowest-entropy tokens degrades performance.

paper: llm/routing/Adaptive-RAG. Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question
reason: An adaptive RAG framework that chooses between no-retrieval, single-step and iterative retrieval per query — a RAG architecture, not cross-model routing.
summary: Adaptive-RAG: a smaller LM classifier trained on automatically collected labels predicts query complexity and picks between no-retrieval, single-step and iterative retrieval-augmented LLMs, improving overall efficiency and accuracy on open-domain QA.

paper: llm/uncertainty-and-hallucination/DoLa. Decoding by Contrasting Layers Improves Factuality in Large Language Models
reason: A decoding strategy whose stated goal is reducing hallucinations and improving factuality, which matches the hallucination folder's scope more closely than efficiency or architecture.
summary: DoLa: contrasting later-layer against earlier-layer logits at decoding time reduces hallucinations without retrieval or fine-tuning, improving LLaMA family models on TruthfulQA by 12-17% absolute points.

paper: ml-foundations/classical-ml/An Introduction to Locally Linear Embedding
reason: LLE is a classical unsupervised dimensionality-reduction algorithm, which this folder's scope names explicitly.
summary: Locally linear embedding: an unsupervised algorithm that maps high-dimensional data into a single global low-dimensional coordinate system by preserving local linear reconstructions of neighbours, with optimizations free of local minima.

paper: ml-foundations/evaluation-and-model-selection/Random Search for Hyper-Parameter Optimization
reason: Hyper-parameter optimization is model selection (the paper's own keyword) and no folder is dedicated to hyper-parameter search; deep-learning/optimizers-and-schedules is the nearest alternative.
summary: Random search: random trials beat grid search for hyper-parameter optimization because only a few hyper-parameters matter per data set, matching or exceeding grid-tuned neural networks in a small fraction of the compute and equalling manually tuned deep belief networks on four of seven data sets over a 32-dimensional space.

paper: ml-foundations/tabular/TabPFN. A Transformer That Solves Small Tabular Classification Problems in a Second
reason: A tabular foundation model for small-dataset classification, which the tabular folder's scope names explicitly (tabular transformers, tabular foundation models).
summary: TabPFN: a Transformer pretrained on synthetic datasets from a causal prior classifies small tabular datasets in-context in under a second, outperforming boosted trees and matching AutoML with up to 230x speedup (5700x on GPU).

paper: ml-systems/distributed-training/Large Scale Distributed Deep Networks
reason: A framework and algorithms for training deep networks across clusters of thousands of machines — cluster-scale distributed training.
summary: DistBelief: Downpour asynchronous SGD and Sandblaster distributed L-BFGS train a deep network 30x larger than previously reported on tens of thousands of CPU cores, reaching state of the art on ImageNet with 16 million images and 21k categories.

paper: ml-systems/inference-and-serving/FlexGen. High-Throughput Generative Inference of Large Language Models with a Single GPU
reason: An LLM inference engine focused on throughput under limited GPU memory (offloading, batching, cache compression) fits the serving folder's scope more closely than llm/efficiency.
summary: FlexGen: offloading across GPU, CPU and disk via a linear-programming search plus 4-bit compression of weights and attention cache runs OPT-175B on a single 16GB GPU at 1 token/s with an effective batch size of 144.

paper: ml-systems/production-ml/Model Cards for Model Reporting
reason: Proposes model documentation centred on disaggregated evaluation across demographic and intersectional groups, which is where a reader would look alongside fairness and bias work; no dedicated model-documentation/transparency folder exists.
summary: Model Cards: short documents accompanying released models that report benchmarked performance across cultural, demographic, phenotypic and intersectional groups together with intended use and evaluation procedures, illustrated with cards for a smiling-face detector and a toxic-comment detector.

paper: nlp/generation-metrics/MAUVE. Measuring the Gap Between Neural Text and Human Text using Divergence Frontiers
reason: MAUVE is an automatic metric for generated text, alongside BLEU and BERTScore.
summary: MAUVE: compares the distribution of generated text to human text with divergence frontiers computed in a quantized embedding space, correlating with human judgments across three open-ended generation tasks.

paper: nlp/pretrained-language-models/Revisiting Few-sample BERT Fine-tuning
reason: A study of fine-tuning BERT and its instability in few-sample settings, which falls under BERT-era encoders and fine-tuning them.
summary: Few-sample BERT fine-tuning: instability traced to a non-standard optimizer with biased gradient estimation, poorly applicable parts of the network and too few pre-determined training iterations; fixing these makes recently proposed stabilization methods matter much less.

paper: nlp/tasks-and-methods/Bad Characters. Imperceptible NLP Attacks
reason: Adversarial examples against text models in general (machine translation, search engines), not LLM-specific jailbreaks or prompt injection, so it sits with adversarial examples.
summary: Bad Characters: imperceptible encoding perturbations (invisible characters, homoglyphs, reorderings, deletions) attack NLP systems in a black-box setting, where a single injection significantly reduces the performance of vulnerable models and three functionally break most of them, including deployed Microsoft and Google systems.

paper: recommender-systems/collaborative-filtering/BPR. Bayesian Personalized Ranking from Implicit Feedback
reason: A pairwise ranking criterion for implicit-feedback item recommendation, applied to matrix factorization and kNN — the core models of the collaborative-filtering folder.
summary: BPR: a maximum-posterior pairwise ranking criterion (BPR-Opt) for implicit feedback, trained by SGD with bootstrap sampling, that outperforms standard learning for matrix factorization and adaptive kNN on personalized ranking.

paper: recommender-systems/deep-and-sequential/DeepFM. A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction
reason: The paper is a CTR-prediction model, which this folder's scope names explicitly; recommender-systems/deep-and-sequential is the close alternative.
summary: DeepFM: a factorization machine and a deep network sharing one raw-feature input learn low- and high-order feature interactions end to end for CTR prediction, with no feature engineering, unlike Wide & Deep.

paper: reinforcement-learning/world-models/Diffusion for World Modeling. Visual Details Matter in Atari
reason: A reinforcement learning agent trained inside a diffusion world model, which is what the world-models folder covers; diffusion is the means, not the topic.
summary: DIAMOND: an RL agent trained entirely in a diffusion world model that preserves visual details reaches a mean human normalized score of 1.46 on Atari 100k, and the same model works as an interactive neural game engine for Counter-Strike: Global Offensive.

paper: representation-learning/embeddings/ArcFace. Additive Angular Margin Loss for Deep Face Recognition
reason: A margin-based softmax loss for learning discriminative face embeddings is metric learning, which this folder covers; it fits more closely than vision architectures and tasks.
summary: ArcFace: an additive angular margin on softmax for discriminative face embeddings, with K sub-centers per class to isolate noisy faces and identity-preserving face synthesis from the pretrained model using only gradients and BN priors.

paper: research-practice/Can large language models provide useful feedback on research papers. A large-scale empirical
reason: The paper studies LLM-generated peer-review feedback on manuscripts, a question about how research is reviewed and done rather than about LLM capabilities per se.
summary: LLM feedback on research papers: GPT-4's comments overlap with human reviewers (30.85% Nature, 39.23% ICLR) about as much as two humans overlap with each other, and 57.4% of 308 surveyed researchers found them helpful or very helpful.

paper: robotics-and-embodied/Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
reason: Robot imitation learning for bimanual manipulation with a teleoperation hardware system — squarely robot learning.
summary: ALOHA/ACT: a <$20k bimanual teleoperation system plus Action Chunking with Transformers, a generative model over action sequences, learns 6 fine manipulation tasks at 80-90% success from 10 minutes of demonstrations.

paper: search-and-ranking/ads/Practical Lessons from Predicting Clicks on Ads at Facebook
reason: CTR prediction for Facebook ads is squarely within computational advertising.
summary: Facebook ad click prediction: decision trees feeding logistic regression beat either alone by over 3%, with historical user/ad features mattering far more than data freshness, learning rate schema or sampling.

paper: search-and-ranking/click-models-and-unbiased-ltr/Unbiased Learning to Rank Meets Reality. Lessons from Baidu's Large-Scale Search Dataset
reason: An empirical test of unbiased learning-to-rank from clicks on a real search dataset, which is exactly this folder's scope.
summary: ULTR on Baidu-ULTR: standard unbiased learning-to-rank techniques robustly improve click prediction but do not consistently improve ranking on expert relevance annotations, with ranking loss and query-document features making stark differences.

paper: search-and-ranking/evaluation/Information Retrieval System Evaluation. Effort, Sensitivity, and Reliability
reason: It studies significance testing, metric reliability and assessor effort in building IR test collections, which is the scope of the IR evaluation folder.
summary: IR significance testing revisited: the t-test is more reliable than the sign or Wilcoxon test and far more reliable than a large percentage difference, and assessor effort is better spent on more topics, each assessed in less detail.

paper: search-and-ranking/indexing-and-classical-ir/SIMD Compression and the Intersection of Sorted Integers
reason: Inverted-index posting-list compression and intersection belong under indexes and compression in classical IR.
summary: S4-BP128-D4 and SIMD Galloping: SIMD-vectorized integer compression decoding at as little as 0.7 CPU cycles per 32-bit integer, plus vectorized posting-list intersection that can double the speed of a state-of-the-art approach for conjunctive queries on GOV2 and ClueWeb09.

paper: search-and-ranking/learning-to-rank/Accuracy at the Top
reason: It proposes a learning algorithm with a convex surrogate loss for precision at the top of a ranked list, motivated by search engines, which fits ranking losses better than classifier evaluation.
summary: Accuracy at the Top: a classification accuracy defined on the top τ-quantile of scores, optimized through a convex surrogate solved as a set of convex problems, with margin-based guarantees and better precision at the top than competing algorithms in most bipartite experiments.

paper: search-and-ranking/neural-ranking/Pretrained Transformers for Text Ranking. BERT and Beyond
reason: A survey of transformer-based text ranking whose scope spans BERT rerankers and dense retrieval; the neural-ranking folder is where a reader would look for the BERT-reranking survey, with dense-retrieval the close second.
summary: Pretrained Transformers for Text Ranking: a survey of transformer rankers split into multi-stage rerankers and dense retrieval, organised around handling long documents and the effectiveness-efficiency tradeoff.

paper: search-and-ranking/search-systems/Beyond Ranking. Optimizing Whole-Page Presentation
reason: Scope explicitly covers whole-page presentation of search results across verticals, which is the paper's subject.
summary: Whole-page presentation: a framework that learns content-aware SERP layouts (positions, image sizes, fonts) for heterogeneous results from data, outperforming a leading federated search presentation algorithm on real data.

paper: trustworthy-ml/ai-safety/AI Control. Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion
reason: Safety protocols for deploying an untrusted, possibly scheming model — a general AI safety/control problem rather than an LLM-specific attack such as jailbreaks or prompt injection.
summary: AI Control: safety protocols tested against an untrusted GPT-4 that intentionally tries to subvert them by backdooring code, where trusted editing by GPT-3.5 and collusion-resistant untrusted monitoring improve substantially on simple baselines.

paper: vision-and-multimodal/vision/Mask R-CNN
reason: Instance segmentation and object detection framework, which falls squarely under vision architectures and tasks (detection, segmentation).
summary: Mask R-CNN: a mask-prediction branch added in parallel to Faster R-CNN's box branch gives instance segmentation at 5 fps and top single-model results on all three COCO tracks.
